name: The Reject Pile
why_it_works: What a brand throws away says more about its standards than anything it keeps. Showing the rejects makes quality concrete: the viewer sees the line, sees what failed it, and trusts what passed.

hook.pattern: Show a pile of rejects and say the reject rate out loud.
examples: We threw all of this out this week.
This is our reject pile. Look closer.

variables.name: check_step
variables.description: The quality check, starting with a verb ending in -ing

variables.name: reject_reason
variables.example: a single chipped or underdeveloped bean

variables.name: offer
variables.description: How to buy, a full sentence starting with a capital
variables.example: Order this week's batch before Sunday

variables.name: batch_rejects
variables.description: How much of one batch gets rejected, worked out from the reject rate

variables.name: spot_tip
variables.description: One sign of a bad one buyers can check themselves, as a sentence
variables.example: Look for beans with uneven color or chips

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, from compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

beats.voiceover: We threw all of this out this week.

visual.prompt: Large messy pile of rejected {{product}} in a bin on the {{brand}} work table, overhead fluorescent light, honest and unstyled, vertical 9:16

Macro shot of one rejected {{product}} item held between two fingers showing {{reject_reason}}, clean white background, vertical 9:16

beats.voiceover: What's left is what you get.

visual.prompt: Neat tray of perfect {{product}} beside the reject bin, {{brand}} label visible, warm light, vertical 9:16

craft.notes: The pile is the hook, so make it physically big and real. One reject shown up close teaches the viewer what to look for, which turns them into a judge who agrees with your standard.

do_not: Show waste in a way that looks careless; say what happens to rejects if they are donated or composted
compliance: Supplements: quality-check claims must be true and documented; no claims that the product treats, cures or prevents any disease; include the FDA structure/function disclaimer if any benefit is mentioned
Do not imply third-party testing or certification you do not hold
